evidence.quote: Our aim is to constrain some of the properties of potential planets embedded in the disk, assuming that they induce the observed rings and gaps.

claims.hypothesis: Two embedded planets, not one, are needed to explain both the inner and the newly resolved outer ring
claims.experiment: Compared one-planet (I, II) and two-planet (III-VII) FARGO3D plus RADMC-3D models with the combined ALMA image via normalised radial profiles
claims.result: One-planet models deviate by more than 3 sigma (model I up to 133 sigma); two-planet models IV-VII are within 3 sigma

evidence.quote: the models with a single planet have an above-significant deviation ($>3\sigma$) from the observation, while the models with two planets IV-VII have a deviation of less than $3\sigma$ in the radial profile

claims.hypothesis: The initial gas surface density profile affects the inner-to-outer ring brightness ratio
claims.experiment: Ran power-law (models I, III) and self-similar (models II, IV) initial profiles
claims.result: The power-law model III overestimates the outer ring peak intensity relative to the inner ring by a factor of 86; model IV reproduces the ratio
claims.finding: An exponentially tapered (self-similar) initial profile is needed

evidence.quote: To match the very low brightness of the outer structure relative to the inner ring, the initial disk gas surface density profile needs to follow an exponentially tapered power law (self-similar solution), rather than a simple power-law profile.

claims.hypothesis: Planet masses and orbits can be constrained by matching the ALMA continuum
claims.experiment: Planet radii and masses from the radial profile and gap-width relations, then tested in seven FARGO3D and RADMC-3D model setups
claims.result: Model VII (alpha = 1e-3, self-similar profile) gives the best agreement and an azimuthally symmetric outer ring, with inner planet 8 M_Jup at 13 au and outer 3 M_Jup at 143 au
claims.finding: The best matching setup has inner planet 8 M_Jup at 13 au and outer planet 3 M_Jup at 143 au

evidence.quote: Consequently, model VII leads to the best agreement between our synthetic observation and the real one.

claims.hypothesis: The outer planet needs to be old and massive to produce the outer ring
claims.experiment: Delayed the outer planet by 6e5 yr (model V) and tapered its mass over 6e5 yr (model VI)
claims.result: Models IV, V and VI all stay within 3 sigma; a 1.7 M_Jup planet that began forming 140 Kyr before the end still induces the outer ring
claims.finding: Outer planet mass can be as low as 1.7-3 M_Jup, lower than earlier estimates, with formation timing not strongly constrained

evidence.quote: This means that the outer planets mass of $1.7 M_{\rm{Jup}}$ in model V, where the planet started to form very recently ($140\,$Kyr before the end of the simulation), is sufficient to successfully induce the outer substructure.

claims.hypothesis: The disk viscosity can be constrained by the symmetry of the outer ring
claims.experiment: Compared alpha = 1e-4 models with alpha = 1e-3 model VII
claims.result: Low alpha gives an asymmetric outer ring with strong accumulation absent in the ALMA image; alpha = 1e-3 gives a symmetric ring
claims.finding: Favours alpha of about 1e-3 or higher, though the asymmetry at low alpha may be an artefact of not modelling planetary accretion

evidence.quote: Our study favors a (cite: s73) disk viscosity of $\alpha\gtrsim10^{-3}$ because we searched for an $\alpha$ that avoids asymmetric accumulations in the outer ring
we suspect that this accumulation is an artifact of not simulating the accretion of the surrounding material onto the planet.

why_this_data.value: Recent ALMA observations resolve the faint outer ring suggested in earlier work

evidence.quote: we calibrated and analyzed recent ALMA observations of the system to identify the main features and focused on resolving the outer ring that was suggested in (cite: w14; p15).

why_this_method.value: Assume planet-disk interaction drives the observed substructures and model it with hydrodynamics plus radiative transfer

evidence.quote: in this work we assume the planet-disk interaction to be the main driver for the observed substructures of HD 100546

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-planet models I and II rejected because they produce no outer ring

evidence.quote: However, these models do not create an outer ring because there is no second planet that might induce an outer trap.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Power-law initial gas profile rejected because the outer ring comes out too bright relative to the inner ring

evidence.quote: In model III the outer structures are relatively bright compared to the inner ring, which is strongly overestimated

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Other ring-forming mechanisms (dead-zone edge, ice lines, magnetic disk winds) are mentioned but not tested

evidence.quote: in this work we assume the planet-disk interaction to be the main driver for the observed substructures of HD 100546

how_they_decided_enough.value: Iterated model setups until normalised radial profiles were within 3 sigma and the outer ring was azimuthally symmetric

evidence.quote: Its normalized radial profile resides within a frame of $3\sigma$ around the detection.
we tested different planet setup scenarios until we reached the best possible agreement between the synthetic and real observations by comparing their respective images and radial profiles

limitations_admitted.value: Planet accretion not simulated; accumulation near the outer planet may be an artefact

evidence.quote: the actual physical accretion process is ignored in this present work, that is, there is no mass transfer from the dust or gas fluids onto the planet.
We also fixed the planets orbit and neglected its potential migration.
In our current approach, however, we modeled gas and dust evolution simultaneously, but we neglected dust growth.

limitations_admitted.value: Simulations run for 0.74 Myr rather than the system age because of computational cost

evidence.quote: However, a simulation of such a duration is computationally unfeasible because we need to choose a high grid resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Inner planet orbit could not be taken from a resolved local minimum

evidence.quote: Because we were unable to resolve the corresponding local minimum, we reverted to the estimated planet position from previous studies

limitations_admitted.value: One planet per gap is a simplification

evidence.quote: It is important to note that the assumption that exactly one planet is responsible for each gap is a simplification.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model selection is by eye over seven hand-picked setups with a 3 sigma criterion; no parameter grid, likelihood or uncertainties on planet mass or radius
Planet masses are largely set by the gap-width formula (lowest K) and the Crida/Lodato floor, so the results depend on the assumed K, alpha and temperature rather than a fit
The inner planet radius (13 au) is inherited from earlier work and not measured here
Observation log table program IDs differ from those in the text
Radial-profile sigma and the effect of image-plane normalisation on the comparison are not described
Degeneracy between alpha, planet mass and formation timing is only partly explored

missing_for_reproduction: tclean and imaging parameters for the SB, LB and combined images
FARGO3D temperature, aspect ratio and numerical setup, and the modified mass-taper code
RADMC-3D and galario settings, and the model inclination and PA
Radial profile extraction and sigma definition used in the model comparison
Resolution of the program ID discrepancy between text and observation table
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 50-150 GB of raw ALMA data for the three execution blocks (one extended with 10.8 km baselines and two compact), with the 2D FARGO3D runs needing substantial compute but small data products
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA data are public and self-calibration intervals are given, and the simulation grid and main parameters are tabulated, but imaging parameters, FARGO3D thermal setup, the modified code, and the profile-comparison details are missing, and the model comparison is manual
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Imaging recipe and simulation setup are incomplete and model selection is a manual iteration, so the main numbers (13 au/8 M_Jup, 143 au/3 M_Jup) could not be rederived without extra choices
